items.title: Neal Caine interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, September 26, 2019
items.q: I was lucky enough to play with Elvin Jones and his band for three or four years, and Betty Carter.

ctx.x: And do you notice any difference between, well I guess I should ask if you’ve played with seat-of-the-pants-learning graduates.

Well I mean I was lucky enough to play with Elvin Jones and his band for three or four years, and Betty Carter. And I got to play with Cedar Walton a couple of times, and Ellis Marsalis. I mean you know I don’t want to generalize too much because I didn’t go to music school. I think a lot of people who go to music school –- it’s weird because I’m all for education in general. But it sounds weird to say that maybe not jazz school has messed up jazz but if you do go through that program, which you have to be a real…
Were you in — I don’t know if this is the right word, were you intimidated going into the Elvin Jones gig?
